purpose: Prove the crawler ANSWERS native browser dialogs with intent rather than letting Playwright auto-dismiss them: a funnel confirm() is accepted and the journey advances, a leave warning is dismissed and the journey survives, an alert is acknowledged, a destructive confirm is refused without an operator approval, and a prompt is declined rather than answered with invented input.
targeted_defect: BUG-M15-DIALOG-AUTODISMISS — the crawler attached no page.on('dialog') listener, so Playwright's documented default applied and EVERY native dialog was auto-dismissed. A confirm-gated 'Continue' therefore answered CANCEL on every crawl of every application: location.href never ran, the action recorded outcome 'none', and a working funnel was indistinguishable from a dead button. The bug is invisible in the DOM — capture of this page is identical before and after the fix — which is why it needs a behavioural fixture rather than an inventory assertion.

expect_controls.why: the funnel actuator whose confirm() must be ACCEPTED
raises a leave warning that must be DISMISSED
a native confirm is not an approved crossing; refused without an A4.3 grant
raises no dialog at all — proves the dialog path is not taken indiscriminately

describes_runtime_behaviour.behaviour: clicking Continue accepts a confirm() and lands on step2.html
clicking Return to dashboard dismisses a leave warning and stays on index.html
every dialog decision is recorded as a browser_event with its type, message, action, intent and reason

lane_note: Both lanes read the same INVENTORY_JS contract; only the Playwright lane can adjudicate the BEHAVIOURAL expectations above, because jsdom has no dialog primitive. Those are declared playwright-only and are exercised by tests/browser/test_page_lifecycle_execution.py rather than by the capture assertions.
